blocks.heading: Draw it
lines: Two sets: four regions (only A, only B, both, neither).
Three sets: eight regions (three 'only', three 'exactly two', all three, none).
Fill the centre first, then the 'exactly two' regions, then the 'only' regions.

blocks.heading: Formulas
lines: Two sets: A or B = A + B - both.
Three sets: at least one = A + B + C - (AB + BC + CA) + all three, where AB counts everyone in both A and B.
A + B + C = exactly one + 2 × exactly two + 3 × all three.
Total = none + exactly one + exactly two + all three.

blocks.heading: Read the wording
lines: 'Both A and B' usually includes people in all three. 'Only A and B' does not.
'At most one' includes the none group. 'At least two' includes all three.

blocks.heading: Largest and smallest values
lines: Write the region you want in terms of one or two free regions.
Push the free regions to their limits.
Then check that every region stays at zero or more, or above any stated minimum.
Fill the whole diagram for the extreme case to confirm it works.

blocks.heading: Common traps
lines: Using a 'both A and B' figure as 'exactly two' when it includes the centre.
Leaving out the none group when matching the total.
